title: We Love the Venerable House
description: We Love the Venerable House in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Ralph Waldo Emerson wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 423, “The House Our Fathers Built to God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We love the ven-er-a-ble house Our fa-thers built to God; In heaven are kept their grate-ful vows, Their dust en-dears the sod.

lines: In heaven are kept their grateful vows,
Here holy thoughts a light have shed
And prayers of tender hope have spread
And anxious hearts have pondered here
And prayed the Eternal Spirit clear
Their doubts and aid their strife.
And in the church a blessing found,
For faith, and peace, and mighty love,
Showed them the life of heaven above
They live with God, their homes are dust;
And, in this fleeting lifetime, trust
On him who by the altar stands,
Speak through his lips Thy pure commands,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Ralph Waldo Emerson died in 1882.
credits: Words by Ralph Waldo Emerson (1803–1882), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
